Policy.description: How a worker admits one offloaded unit: a machine offers itself (headroom) when its smallest unit fits (`smallestMegabytes`), the free memory it reports is what a unit may still take above its floor, and a unit is admitted when its own predicted peak fits into that. Raised memory pressure (`warn`) alone refuses only units above `warnMaximumMegabytes` and every unit while swap is growing; critical pressure refuses all. While the readiness stage of the machine runs (a fresh claim that does not wait) the machine runs at most `stageConcurrency` remote units at once: the stage reads the project graph through the fleet cache, and a lookup that waits for a thread starved by compiles took 9 s instead of 5 ms (measured on a 16 GB worker with 3 to 6 remote units beside its stage).
